Durchlauchtigster Fürst

Gnädigster Herr!

Noch immer sehe ich die Ankunft der Oder und Nezzbrücher Leute entgegen. Von meinen einmahl entworfenen Plan gehn ich nicht ab, und ich stehe davor daß keine Hufe unter 600 rt / das heißt GrundGeld und Zinsen zusammen genommen / wegegeben werden soll. Ist es nur mit dem allerschlechtesten Gründen geglückt ſo wird es mir bey den Beſſerpre nicht fehlen. Die Taxe wird diese Woche wohl fertig werden, und wie ich hoffe vom der Zagorower Gütern über 400000 rt ausfallen Hierdurch wird allen Unwillen trozz geboten, ich nehme in

Berlin so viel Geld als zur Bezahlung der Ge Schlabrendorff, Lichnowski und anderer drückenden Gläubigern nötig ist und bezahle. Allmählig, kömt für diese Gründe das Geld an man zahlt jene Schuld wieder ab, auf der Art wird nichts durch Übereilung verlohren und das große Ziel ist erreicht. Schwer, sehr schwer, geht es her, denn es ist durch die leichte vorherigen Verkäufe vieles verdorben; indes wird meine Beharrlichkeit siegen, dafür hafte ich.

Der lezthinige Ärger mit Glenck, wo mir der Mensch ins Gesicht sagt ich wolle ihm sein Eigenthum entreißen, und der Verdruß mit den Olesnicer aufgehezten Erbpächtern, hat mir eine fürchter liche Colique zugezogen die mir zwang 3 Tage das Bette zu hüten, ich bin noch sehr Marade.

Ubrigens haben die Wrąbczyner Unterthanen gegen ihren Contract protestirt und weigern sich den Zins abzuführen. Ihre Beschwerde ist, daß ihme Glenck angedroht ihre Gründe abzunehmen, und sie dafür andere geben zu wollen, außer dem Beklagen sie sich daß des Glencks Schreiber, sie durchs ganze Jahr noch zu dienen gezwungen und daß er, da er die Dienste nicht alle auf der Woigdtey brauchen können, die Unterthanen nach Zagorowo geschickt wo sie den Bürgern arbeiten müßen, und wofür

sich der Meyer pro Person / deren 18. sind / täglich 4 gg. bezahlen laßen. die Unterthanen finden dies zu hart, daß man sie wie die Sclaven zum dienen an andere fremde Menschen verkauft. Der Meyer hat die Leute überdem bekannt gemacht, daß er sämtliche 18 Wirthe ganz zur Voigtey ziehen, und daß sie Glenck an den von Marowecki, welcher auf der Art 15000 rt für die Voigtey giebt, mit verkaufen will.

Die Unterthanen flehen daß Ewer Durchlaucht dies nicht gestatten mögten, ſie wollen gerne einen rthlr pro Morgen von ihren Ackern geben, und alles leisten was sonsten in ihren Kräften stände. Ich habe die Menschen mit ihren Geſuchen und Lamentos an dem Justiz Bürgermeister Schenck gewiesen, und dem ersucht sie zu beruhigen und die Sache aufs reine zu bringen damit Glenck nicht wieder schreit, daß ich ihm sein wohl erworbenes Eigenthum entreißen wolle.

translation.en:
149

Most Serene Prince

Most gracious Lord!

Still I await the arrival of the people from the Oder and Netze marshes. From Wednesday onward they will probably present themselves in whole troops, and then I hope to be swiftly at the goal of my wishes. Several plots which the Swięcia people had [uncertain: marked out], and which lay about as waste corners along the border, I have sold very advantageously; I not only place well with a purchaser the soil that was held in no regard at all, but likewise the figure, so as now to be able to conclude better with the large purchasers for regular parcels. From the plan I once drew up I do not depart, and I stand surety that no Hufe shall be given away under 600 Rthl / that is, ground-money and rents taken together /. If it has succeeded with the very worst plots, then it will not fail me with the [uncertain: better ones]. The valuation will probably be finished this week and, as I hope, will come out at over 400000 Rthl for the Zagórów estates. By this means defiance is bidden to all ill-will; I take in

Berlin as much money as is needed for the payment of Schlabrendorff, Lichnowski and other pressing creditors, and pay them. Gradually the money for these plots comes in, and that debt is paid off again; in this way nothing is lost through precipitancy and the great aim is attained. It goes hard, very hard, for much has been spoilt by the easy earlier sales; yet my perseverance will prevail, for that I answer.

The late vexation with Glenck, where the man tells me to my face that I mean to wrest his property from him, and the annoyance with the hereditary leaseholders stirred up by the Oleśnica people, have brought upon me a frightful colic which compelled me to keep my bed for 3 days; I am still very poorly.

For the rest, the Wrąbczyn subjects have protested against their contract and refuse to render the rent. Their complaint is that Glenck threatened [uncertain: them] to take their plots away and to give them others in their place; besides this they complain that Glenck's clerk compelled them to serve through the whole year still, and that he, being unable to use all the services on the village bailiff's holding, sent the subjects to Zagórów, where they must work for the burgesses, and for which

the steward has himself paid 4 Groschen daily per person / of whom there are 18 /. The subjects find this too hard, that they should be sold like slaves to serve other, strange men. The steward has moreover made it known to the people that he will draw all 18 householders entirely to the village bailiff's holding, and that Glenck means to sell them along with it to von Marowecki, who on those terms gives 15000 Rthl for the village bailiff's holding.

The subjects implore that Your Serene Highness might not permit this; they will gladly give one rthlr per Morgen of their fields and render everything else that lies within their power. I have referred the people with their petitions and lamentations to the justice-burgomaster Schenck, and have requested him to quiet them and to bring the matter to a clear issue, so that Glenck may not cry out again that I mean to wrest from him his well-acquired property.

In deepest esteem I remain, until death,

Your Most Serene Highness's

Trąbczyn

the 2nd of December

1804

most humble and obedient servant

v Triebenfeld

Gradually the money for these plots comes in, and that debt is paid off again; in this way nothing is lost through precipitancy and the great aim is attained. It goes hard, very hard, for much has been spoilt by the easy earlier sales; yet my perseverance will prevail, for that I answer.

The late vexation with Glenck, where the man tells me to my face that I mean to wrest his property from him, and the annoyance with the hereditary leaseholders stirred up by the Oleśnica people, have brought upon me a frightful colic which compelled me to keep my bed for 3 days; I am still very poorly.

For the rest, the Wrąbczyn subjects have protested against their contract and refuse to render the rent. Their complaint is that Glenck threatened [uncertain: them] to take their plots away and to give them others in their place; besides this they complain that Glenck's clerk compelled them to serve through the whole year still, and that he, being unable to use all the services on the village bailiff's holding, sent the subjects to Zagórów, where they must work for the burgesses, and for which

the steward has himself paid 4 Groschen daily per person / of whom there are 18 /. The subjects find this too hard, that they should be sold like slaves to serve other, strange men. The steward has moreover made it known to the people that he will draw all 18 householders entirely to the village bailiff's holding, and that Glenck means to sell them along with it to von Marowecki, who on those terms gives 15000 Rthl for the village bailiff's holding.

The subjects implore that Your Serene Highness might not permit this; they will gladly give one rthlr per Morgen of their fields and render everything else that lies within their power. I have referred the people with their petitions and lamentations to the justice-burgomaster Schenck, and have requested him to quiet them and to bring the matter to a clear issue, so that Glenck may not cry out again that I mean to wrest from him his well-acquired property.

In deepest esteem I remain, until death,

Your Most Serene Highness's

Trąbczyn

the 2nd of December

1804

most humble and obedient servant

v Triebenfeld
summary_en: Triebenfeld says he is expecting the people from the Oder and Netze marshes and has sold waste land on the border on favourable terms; no Hufe, he says, is to be given up for less than 600 Rthl. He hopes the valuation of the Zagórów estates will come to more than 400000 Rthl, and intends to raise money in Berlin for Schlabrendorff and Lichnowski. The Wrąbczyn subjects, he reports, are refusing the rent, complaining of Glenck's threats and of forced services for citizens of Zagórów, and offering one Rthl per Morgen; he referred them to justice-burgomaster Schenck.
summary_de: Triebenfeld erwartet die Leute aus dem Oder- und Netzebruch und hat wüste Gründe an der Grenze vorteilhaft verkauft; keine Hufe soll unter 600 Rthl abgegeben werden. Er hofft, die Taxe der Zagorower Güter ergebe über 400000 Rthl, und will in Berlin Geld für Schlabrendorff und Lichnowski aufnehmen. Die Wrąbczyner Untertanen verweigern den Zins, klagen über Glencks Drohungen und Zwangsdienste bei Zagorower Bürgern und bieten einen Rthl pro Morgen; er verwies sie an Justiz Bürgermeister Schenck.

reading.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Trąbczyn to the Prince. He is waiting for settlers from the Oder and Netze Brüche and has sold waste plots at the border. His price floor is 600 rt per Hufe. He hopes the Taxe of the Zagorower estates will come to over 400000 rt, and he will borrow in Berlin to pay Schlabrendorff and Lichnowski. He has quarrelled with Glenck, has had colic, and has trouble with the Oleśnica Erbpächter. The Wrąbczyn subjects refuse their Zins and complain that Glenck threatened to take their plots, that Glenck's Schreiber forced them to serve and that the Meyer hired 18 of them out to Zagorowo burghers at 4 gg a day. The Meyer has also told them they are to be sold with the Voigtey to Marowecki for 15000 rt. They offer one rthlr per Morgen, and Triebenfeld has sent them to Justiz Bürgermeister Schenck.
